evaluation.positioning_hook: A scarred runaway with a hidden body-count hunts the people who erased her orphanage, while a jaded fixer and a compromised partner close in on the last surviving child.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The hook is immediate and genre-legible: a damaged young woman, missing children, and a citywide hunt with a brutal reveal. The audience is real, but the script’s extreme violence, elliptical storytelling, and art-house presentation narrow the commercial lane rather than opening it wide.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The orphanage/missing-children engine lands clearly by the midpoint, and the reveal that Isabella is one of the escaped children gives the premise a clean spine. The opening is more mood-forward than premise-forward, so the hook takes a few pages to fully lock.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Isabella is memorable because she is both predator and wounded child, and Jenny gets a strong moral-pressure arc through David and the job. Luigi is vivid as a sleazy, dangerous operator, but the script is built more around mood and reversal than around deeply layered ensemble durability.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits to a strange, unsettling register: chat-overlay dialogue, cassette-tape nostalgia, scar imagery, and a childlike killer’s emotional logic. That formal and tonal confidence gives it a distinct identity even when the underlying chase structure is familiar.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: Once Jenny and Luigi enter the investigation, the story moves with real urgency toward the park confrontation and the restaurant standoff. The first stretch is more atmospheric than propulsive, but the escalation into the final third is strong and increasingly tense.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The script’s core contradiction — a traumatized escaped child who can kill with a snap, yet still wants connection and a first kiss — is instantly ownable. It feels fresh because the emotional logic and the horror of the premise are fused rather than merely juxtaposed.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: New York is used well as a nocturnal, surveilled space, and the orphanage backstory suggests a larger criminal system. But most of the world exists to service the pursuit, so the setting feels specific without yet becoming richly layered.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a hard-to-mistake tone: mournful, abrasive, and strangely tender, with bursts of dark humor and childlike play. The contrast between Isabella’s innocence and the violence around her is the signature register.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The orphanage, the scars, the missing parents, and Jenny’s hidden attachment to David all imply deeper emotional and institutional history. The script doesn’t fully unpack those layers, but it clearly suggests more beneath the surface than the immediate chase plot.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The Isabella/Jenny/Luigi triangle generates most of the energy, and the David thread adds a useful pressure point. Still, this is not an ensemble engine; it lives on a few charged relationships rather than a broad recurring social system.

lead_characters.name: Isabella
lead_characters.demographics: Female, 18, white, scarred, emotionally arrested, orphaned runaway with a teenage exterior and childlike interior.
lead_characters.hook: Isabella is a scarred, socially stunted young woman who moves through the city like someone half-feral and half-dreaming. She is both the hunted and the hunter, using a terrifying supernatural burst of violence to protect herself while desperately craving intimacy, identity, and a first real human connection.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is showcase territory in the vein of Jodie Comer in Killing Eve or Anya Taylor-Joy in The Witch: a role that lets an actor play fragility, menace, shame, and sudden power in the same breath. The big draw is the contradiction — she can be terrifying and heartbreakingly childlike in adjacent beats.

lead_characters.name: Jenny
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 20s, scarred, guarded, queer-coded, working within a criminal/paramilitary structure.
lead_characters.hook: Jenny is a controlled, watchful fixer who starts as an operator and gradually reveals a private moral fracture. Her connection to David gives her a human tether, and her scenes with Isabella force her to confront what she has been helping to erase.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Alicia Vikander in Ex Machina or Rebecca Ferguson in Mission: Impossible a chance to play cool precision with a buried emotional current. The showcase is the slow reveal of conscience under discipline, especially in the restaurant and final bedroom scenes.

lead_characters.name: Luigi
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 30s, streetwise, sexually aggressive, armed enforcer.
lead_characters.hook: Luigi is a smirking, crude, predatory handler who treats violence like routine and women like a joke until the situation turns on him. He is useful as a pressure-cooker antagonist because his confidence masks real fear the moment Isabella stops behaving like prey.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of scene-eating supporting turn that actors use to announce danger, like Walton Goggins in Justified or Ben Mendelsohn in Animal Kingdom. The role offers swagger, menace, and a humiliating collapse when the power dynamic flips.

lead_characters.name: Aiden
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 20s, Black, soft-spoken, emotionally open, later revealed as a trap.
lead_characters.hook: Aiden reads first as Isabella’s possible first safe connection: shy, observant, and disarmingly gentle. The turn into betrayal makes him less a character than a devastating emotional test for Isabella’s capacity to trust.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor do tenderness and threat in one package, similar to Lakeith Stanfield in short-form emotional reversals or Daniel Kaluuya in a scene that flips audience trust. The showcase is the pivot from warmth to menace.

lead_characters.name: David
lead_characters.demographics: Male, mid-teens, timid voice, off-screen/voice presence, vulnerable.
lead_characters.hook: David is mostly a voice and a pressure point, but he matters because he gives Jenny a reason to keep choosing the mission over the job. He functions as the emotional hostage in the story’s moral geometry.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is not a flashy role, but it gives a young actor the chance to play vulnerability with real stakes, similar to the off-screen emotional weight of a key child in a thriller. The value is in making the audience feel the cost of Jenny’s choices.

technical.vfx_details: A few body-explosion moments and blood-splatter enhancements; otherwise largely practical.
technical.sfx_needs: Blood effects, practical gunfire, scar makeup continuity, body-disintegration gore beats.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: limited theatrical or streamer original with genre positioning.

budget.note: Contemporary New York locations, limited cast, and only minor gore/VFX keep this in contained-feature territory; the main cost pressure is night exteriors and subway/park access.

casting.note: The lead requires an actor who can play innocence, erotic curiosity, menace, and trauma without losing coherence. Jenny and Luigi also need performers who can carry long dialogue exchanges and sudden shifts in power.

development.note: The script’s elliptical structure and stylized dialogue are part of the appeal, but the opening takes time to clarify the orphanage/missing-children engine. Buyers will weigh that delay against the strength of the final-third reveal.

comp_set.why_it_comps: The cold, unsettling emotional register and the sense of characters behaving according to a private, disturbing logic are close to this script’s DNA.

audience_target.primary_audience: Adult genre viewers who like elevated, unsettling thrillers with a strong female lead and a bleak emotional core.
audience_target.demographics: 18-44 skew, slightly female-leaning, streamer-native, art-house genre audience with appetite for dark material.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary urban locations, a small cast, and limited practical gore keep this in indie-feature range, with night shoots and location access as the main scope drivers.

lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane where mood, performance, and a sharp central conceit matter as much as plot mechanics. It is the kind of script that can attract a director with a strong visual voice and a lead actor looking for a risky, signature turn.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature: Isabella’s story resolves as a single revenge/escape arc, and Jenny’s thread closes with the rescue of David rather than opening a clean sequel or spinoff vector.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Isabella is a killer with childlike longing.
strengths.what_it_means: That contradiction gives the movie a real commercial hook: the audience gets horror, empathy, and suspense from the same character. It is the kind of role that can attract a bold young lead looking for a signature breakout turn.
strengths.evidence: The carousel scene, the first-kiss fixation, and the final bedroom sequence where she laughs at Luigi dancing naked all come from the same emotional engine.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The orphanage mystery gives the chase a spine.
strengths.what_it_means: The missing-children backstory turns the film from a generic pursuit into a revenge-and-revelation engine with a clear moral wound. That makes the premise easier to sell to genre buyers who want a hook that is both emotional and plot-driven.
strengths.evidence: The 404’d orphanage pages, the posters of missing children, and the reveal that the escaped children are being hunted all sharpen the central question.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tone is singular and hard to mistake.
strengths.what_it_means: The script’s blend of tenderness, disgust, and dark humor gives it a distinct identity in a crowded elevated-thriller market. Buyers looking for something that feels authored rather than generic will notice that immediately.
strengths.evidence: The chat-overlay dialogue, cassette-tape soundtrack cues, and Isabella’s sudden laughter during the hostage scene create a very specific register.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The city is used as a pressure system.
strengths.what_it_means: New York is not just backdrop here; it becomes a surveillance maze that supports the thriller mechanics without requiring expensive world-building. That helps the script stay attractive to indie financiers and streamer buyers alike.
strengths.evidence: Subway platforms, tunnels, empty streets, and Central Park all function as pursuit corridors and concealment spaces.

whats_special.headline: This is a contained, performance-forward thriller with a genuinely ownable lead role and a clean emotional engine under the horror. The indie-scale location footprint and limited cast make it packageable for streamer originals or boutique genre financiers, while the Isabella contradiction gives it breakout-actor appeal.

items.area: The opening delays the premise reveal.
items.detail: The first stretch is heavily mood-led before the orphanage/missing-children engine fully clicks. That is a real development conversation because buyers will compare the script’s atmospheric opening to the clarity and urgency of the final-third reveal.

Her snap-triggered body explosions are striking, but the script does not define the mechanism or limits in a way that creates a stable rule set. That keeps the film in a more poetic lane, but it also narrows the audience that wants a cleaner genre contract.

items.area: The dialogue leans stylized over naturalistic.
items.detail: The chat overlays, repeated phrasing, and heightened exchanges give the script voice, but they also make some scenes feel written rather than lived. A buyer will see that as part of the aesthetic, while also recognizing it as a taste-specific lane.

items.area: The supporting cast is thin by design.
items.detail: Jenny, Luigi, Aiden, and David are functional and vivid, but the film is not building a broad relationship web. That keeps the focus tight, but it also means the project lives or dies on the lead performance and the central conceit.

issues.headline: The main friction is not the premise but the presentation: the script withholds its engine early and leans into a stylized register that will be polarizing outside the elevated-genre lane. It is strongest when the emotional contradiction and the orphanage mystery are in the same frame, and weakest when it asks the audience to live in atmosphere alone.
